sections.title: Turning an action into a descriptive adjective
sections.content: In Hungarian, adding *-ó* or *-ő* to a verb stem creates the present participle (*folyamatos melléknévi igenév*). It describes an ongoing activity or characteristic and functions just like an ordinary adjective before a noun. In English, this often corresponds to adjectives ending in "-ing" (e.g. *dolgozó* = working, *vezető* = leading/executive).

items.spanish: Sok dolgozó ember érkezik az irodába nyolc órakor.
items.english: Many working people arrive at the office at eight o'clock.

items.spanish: Péter vezető beosztásban dolgozik a cégnél.
items.english: Péter works in a managerial position at the company.
We are looking for an English-speaking colleague.

sections.content: Remember vowel harmony: back-vowel verb stems take *-ó* (*dolgoz* → *dolgozó*, *olvas* → *olvasó*), while front-vowel verb stems take *-ő* (*él* → *élő*, *kérdez* → *kérdező*). When placed before a noun, the participle does not take plural *-k* (*dolgozó emberek*, not *dolgozók emberek*).
